before.text:
1. Introduction
                                                Katz and Sarnak [KS] have introduced the idea of a family of L–functions with an
                                             associated symmetry type. The symmetry type has been shown to govern the distribution
                                             and spacing of zeros in the function field case [KS2], and there is strong numerical evidence
                                             [Ru] that it governs the behavior of zeros in more general cases. The paper [ILS] also shows
                                             clear evidence that the symmetry type governs the distribution of low–lying zeros of a wide
                                             variety of L–functions. In this paper we give evidence that the symmetry type of a family
                                             of L–functions governs the behavior of mean values of the L–functions.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Integrality is proved locally at every prime-power scale: factorial products become floor-sum valuations, and each scale contribution is forced to be a nonnegative integer.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source regroups products of factorials and odd double factorials, evaluates their p-adic valuations as sums over p^ell, and obtains formulas for v_p(g_{k,U}) and v_p(g_{k,O}). The orthogonal summand is bounded below using M^2-M>=0 for integral M. The unitary summand splits into the two possible residue cases for floor((2k-1)/p^ell), and in each case is an integer greater than -1, hence nonnegative. The symplectic result is transferred through g_{k+1,O}=2^k g_{k,Sp}.
directed.conceptual_reading: A global divisibility claim is decomposed into independent certificates indexed by prime and scale. The residue split turns opaque factorial cancellation into a finite local obstruction analysis.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Finite products bridge to p-adic valuations via Legendre-style floor sums; completing squares and elementary floor alternatives bridge those sums to termwise nonnegativity.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The detailed proof treats odd primes and dismisses p=2 separately as easy; exact prime-support consequences require additional case checking. Several floor indices are extraction-fragile.
directed.uncertainty: High confidence in the scale-by-scale nonnegativity mechanism, with lower confidence in literal transcription of every displayed floor formula.
